claim: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity in an AWS Region; an AZ is not a single data center.
question: What is an Availability Zone made of: one data center or several?

values.display: one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity
values.spoken: one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity

values.display: one or more discrete data centers

evidence.quote: An Availability Zone (AZ) is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity in an AWS Region.

Each Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers, each with redundant power, networking, and connectivity, and housed in separate facilities. Because they are physically separate, only a single Availability Zone would be affected in the unlikely event of a fire, tornado, or flooding.

claim: AWS can restrict new zonal resources in a constrained Availability Zone and can remove it from the list for new accounts, so two accounts can see a different number of Availability Zones in the same Region.
question: Why can two accounts see a different number of Availability Zones in the same Region?

values.display: a different number of available Availability Zones in a Region than another account does
values.spoken: a constrained Availability Zone can be hidden from new accounts, so the count differs per account

evidence.quote: If this happens, we might restrict you from creating zonal resources in a constrained Availability Zone, unless you already have resources in that Availability Zone. Eventually, we might also remove the constrained Availability Zone from the list of Availability Zones for new accounts. Therefore, your account might have a different number of available Availability Zones in a Region than another account does.

claim: An AZ ID names the same physical location in every AWS account, while for accounts created before November 2025 the AZ code (such as us-east-1a) of the oldest Regions is mapped independently per account.

values.display: the same physical location in every AWS account
values.spoken: an AZ ID is the same physical location in every account

values.display: independently map Availability Zones to codes for each AWS account

qualifiers.condition: independent mapping applies to accounts created before November 2025, in the oldest Regions

evidence.quote: Each Availability Zone has an AZ ID, which is the same physical location in every AWS account.

For accounts created before November 2025, in our oldest Regions, we independently map Availability Zones to codes for each AWS account. For example, the `us-east-1a` Availability Zone for your account might not be the same physical location as it is in another account. Accounts created starting November 2025, get the same Availability Zones mapped to codes.
